chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayoub, from Saif ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the people of Syria worse, or the people of Rome?' He said: 'The Romans disbelieved and were not inimical to us, but the people of Syria disbelieved and were inimical to us.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the people of Syria and the Romans regarding their enmity to the Shia?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the people of Syria (Sham) and the Romans (Rum) based on their specific relationship with the Ahl al-Bayt. While both groups are considered disbelievers (kuffar), the Romans remained neutral and did not actively oppose the Shia, whereas the people of Syria were not only disbelievers but also actively hostile and inimical to them. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the nature of enmity (adawa) rather than mere disbelief (kufr) when evaluating adversaries.
